mainTopic: Mistaken consecration (הקדש בטעות): the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל, and whether בית שמאי really hold a true mistake creates הקדש
overview: The משנה finishes the argument about a person who consecrates something by mistake. בית שמאי say it is הקדש, and בית הלל say it is not. The משנה gives three examples: a black bull that turned out white, a gold coin that turned out silver, and a barrel of wine that turned out to be oil. The גמרא explains that בית שמאי learn the start of הקדש from תמורה, which works even by mistake, while בית הלל say only תמורה works that way. The גמרא then challenges בית שמאי: a תמורה set for a later time waits for that time, so the הקדש should wait to see what really comes out. רב פפא answers that the man meant the first black bull to come out, so even בית שמאי agree that a true mistake does not create הקדש. The case is only called a mistake because his first words were misleading. The גמרא tests this against a משנה about a released נזיר vow and answers that בית הלל had misunderstood בית שמאי's reason. A new challenge from another משנה begins at the end of the עמוד and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: בית הלל: a mistaken consecration does not take effect
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes the argument: בית הלל hold that a consecration made by mistake is not הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: it is not consecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives בית הלל's side of the argument. בית שמאי's side was on the previous עמוד: they hold that a mistaken consecration does take effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two views on a הקדש made by mistake. בית שמאי say the item becomes holy anyway. בית הלל say it does not, because the person did not mean this item.

keyTerms.meaning: Something consecrated, set aside as holy property
The school of הלל, usually the more lenient side

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say: it is not consecrated.
phrases.notes: The first half, where בית שמאי say a mistaken consecration does take effect, is just before this on the previous עמוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the argument that the משנה began on the previous עמוד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to בית הלל, a consecration made by mistake does not take effect.

steps.title: First example: the black bull that turned out white
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains what a mistaken consecration looks like. Someone consecrates the first black bull to leave his house, but a white bull comes out first.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? He said: 'The black bull that leaves my house first is consecrated,' and a white one came out first. בית שמאי say it is consecrated, and בית הלל say it is not consecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'How so?' and gives a clear picture of the argument. A man consecrated the first black bull to leave his house, but the first one out was white.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man named two things: 'black' and 'first.' The white bull fits 'first' but not 'black.' At first reading, בית שמאי seem to say his words still take effect, and בית הלל say he never meant a white bull, so it stays ordinary. The גמרא will later explain more exactly what בית שמאי mean (Step 8).
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two schools here. It is בית שמאי, usually the stricter side, who say there is הקדש here, and בית הלל who say there is not. At first glance this sounds like בית שמאי make the white bull holy, but in Step 8 רב פפא explains that they mean the first black bull to come out, even if a white one came out before it.

phrases.english: How so?
He said: 'A black bull'
that will come out of my house first
is consecrated,'
and a white one came out first,
Beit Shammai say: it is consecrated,
and Beit Hillel say: it is not consecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד? אָמַר שׁוֹר שָׁחוֹר שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִבֵּיתִי רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real example of the argument just stated
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A white bull that came out first, when a black one was consecrated: בית שמאי say it is הקדש, and בית הלל say it is not.

steps.title: More examples: the gold coin and the barrel of wine
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives two more examples with the same argument. A gold dinar turns out to be silver, and a barrel of wine turns out to be oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said, 'The gold dinar that comes into my hand first is consecrated,' and a silver one came up, בית שמאי say it is consecrated and בית הלל say it is not. If he said, 'The barrel of wine that comes into my hand first is consecrated,' and one of oil came up, בית שמאי say it is consecrated and בית הלל say it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same argument with a coin and with a barrel. It shows the argument is not only about animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case has the same pattern: the person names a kind of item and says 'the first one,' and a different kind comes first. Giving several cases shows the argument is a general rule about mistakes in הקדש.
steps.whatToRemember: In all three cases בית שמאי say a mistaken consecration takes effect, and בית הלל say it does not.

phrases.english: 'A gold dinar that will come up'
in my hand first is consecrated,'
and a silver one came up,
Beit Shammai say: it is consecrated,
and Beit Hillel say: it is not consecrated.
'A barrel of wine that will come up'
in my hand first is consecrated,'
and one of oil came up,
Beit Shammai say: it is consecrated,
and Beit Hillel say: it is not consecrated.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּינַר זָהָב שֶׁיַּעֲלֶה בְּיָדִי רִאשׁוֹן הֲרֵי הוּא הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds two more examples that follow the same pattern as the bull
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The same argument applies to coins and barrels: בית שמאי say הקדש, and בית הלל say not הקדש.

steps.title: What is בית שמאי's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks why בית שמאי hold that a mistaken consecration takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'בית שמאי say it is consecrated,' and so on. What is the reason of בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It quotes the start of the משנה and asks for the source behind בית שמאי's view, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an act done by mistake has no effect, so בית שמאי's view is surprising. The גמרא wants to know what they base it on.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that analyzes the משנה
And so on: the quote continues as in the משנה

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים הֶקְדֵּשׁ כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: GEMARA: Beit Shammai say it is consecrated, etc.
What is the reason of Beit Shammai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה to the גמרא's analysis of בית שמאי's view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic for saying that a mistaken הקדש takes effect

steps.title: בית שמאי learn the start of הקדש from תמורה
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי learn the first act of consecrating from תמורה, the later stage of הקדש. Since תמורה works even by mistake, so does a first consecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn the start of הקדש from the end of הקדש. Just as תמורה works even by mistake, so too הקדש works even by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that בית שמאי compare a first consecration to תמורה, which takes effect even when done by mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תמורה means trying to swap an ordinary animal for one that is already holy. It is called the 'end' of הקדש because it comes after the holiness is already there. Since a תמורה takes effect even by mistake, בית שמאי say a first act of הקדש should also work by mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: The start of consecration, making something holy for the first time
The end of consecration, meaning תמורה
Swapping an ordinary animal for a holy one; both end up holy

steps.confusionAlert: A תמורה 'by mistake' means something like this: he meant to name his black bull as the swap but said 'this white bull,' and the white bull still becomes holy.
steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison to תמורה is the base of בית שמאי's whole view. The rest of the סוגיא tests it.

phrases.english: That we derive the beginning of consecration
from the end of consecration.
phrases.notes: 'The end of consecration' means תמורה, a swap made on an animal that is already holy.

phrases.english: Just as substitution takes effect even in error,
so too consecration takes effect even in error.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about בית שמאי's reason
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A comparison: the start of הקדש is learned from תמורה, which works even by mistake.

steps.title: בית הלל: only תמורה works by mistake
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reject the comparison. A mistake works only for תמורה, but we do not bring holiness onto an item for the first time by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: that rule is only for תמורה. But we do not bring הקדש down onto something by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית הלל's reply. They agree that תמורה works by mistake, but they refuse to extend that rule to a first consecration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In תמורה there is already a holy animal in the picture, so the swap can hold even with a mistake. A first consecration creates holiness from nothing, so בית הלל require that it be done on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring down, to place holiness onto something
We do not bring it down

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
This applies only to substitution.
But bringing down consecration in error,
we do not bring it down.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: הָנֵי מִילֵּי תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison that בית שמאי drew from תמורה
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the extension from תמורה to a first הקדש; the rule for תמורה itself stays
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: תמורה builds on holiness that already exists, so it cannot teach a first act of consecration.

steps.title: Challenge to בית שמאי: a delayed תמורה waits for its time
steps.stepSummary: Even using בית שמאי's own comparison, a תמורה set for midday only takes effect at midday. So the הקדש should also wait until it is clear what came out, and a white bull should not become holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to בית שמאי: if someone said, 'This is in place of this at midday,' would it become a תמורה right then? No, it becomes a תמורה only when midday arrives. Here too, the הקדש should take effect only once the matter becomes clear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית שמאי from their own source. Since תמורה follows the person's words about timing, the הקדש should also follow his words and wait to see what really comes out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone sets a תמורה for midday, everyone agrees it waits until midday and does not go against his words. So if a first הקדש is learned from תמורה, it should wait to see what comes out first and take effect only if that is a black bull. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: In place of this one, the wording of a תמורה

phrases.english: And according to Beit Shammai,
just as if one said:
'This is in exchange for this at midday,'
phrases.notes: He is swapping an ordinary animal for a holy one, but says the swap should start at midday.

phrases.english: would it become a substitute from that moment?
Rather, only when midday arrives
does it become a substitute.
So too here,
it should take effect when the matter is revealed!
phrases.notes: He means: wait to see what actually comes out first, and make it holy only if it is a black bull.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְבֵית שַׁמַּאי, מָה אִילּוּ אָמַר הָרֵי זֶה תַּחַת זֶה לַחֲצִי הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to בית שמאי's comparison to תמורה and attacks it from the inside
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's claim that a mistaken הקדש takes effect, based on תמורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תמורה follows the person's words, as shown when it waits until midday. So a הקדש learned from it should also follow his words and apply only if a black bull actually comes out first.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'First' means the first black bull to come out
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the man meant whichever black bull comes out first, not the first bull of any color.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: That is why he said 'first.' He meant: when the first black bull comes out.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge from Step 7. He explains that בית שמאי read the word 'first' as 'the first black bull to come out.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 asked why the black bull should become holy if a white bull came out first. רב פפא answers that the man never meant 'the first bull of all.' He meant 'the first of my black bulls.' So the black bull that came out after the white one really fits his words, and no mistake is involved.

keyTerms.meaning: That is why it was said

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
That is why he said 'first':
phrases.notes: He is talking about the man's words from the משנה: 'the black bull that comes out of my house first.'

phrases.english: when the first [black bull] comes out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 7 by reading the man's words differently.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'First' means the first bull of any color, so a black bull that follows a white one does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'First' means the first black bull, so the black bull becomes holy even if a white bull came out before it.

steps.title: What if he owns only one black bull?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. The משנה seems to cover even a man who has only one black bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he said 'black bull.' Aren't we dealing even with a case where he has only this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's reading. If the man owns only one black bull, 'the first black bull' makes no sense, so 'first' must mean first of all the bulls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's reading only works if the man has several black bulls, because only then can one of them be the 'first black one.' But nothing in the משנה limits the case to an owner of several black bulls. If he has just one, the word 'first' must mean first of all his animals, and we are back to the problem from Step 7.

phrases.english: But he said 'black bull,'
aren't we dealing even
with a case where he has only this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״שׁוֹר שָׁחוֹר״ קָאָמַר, מִי לָא עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's answer from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading that 'first' means first black bull
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's case seems to include an owner with only one black bull. For him, 'first' can only mean first of all the bulls.

steps.title: The case is someone with two or three black bulls
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is speaking about someone who owns several black bulls.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where he has two or three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב פפא. It limits the משנה's case to an owner of two or three black bulls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the man has several black bulls, 'the first black one' is a sensible thing to say. So רב פפא's reading fits, and the challenge from Step 9 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for... (this case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for a case where he has two or three.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא צְרִיכָא, דְּאִית לֵיהּ תְּרֵין תְּלָתָא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה includes an owner with only one black bull.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about an owner with two or three black bulls, so 'first black bull' makes sense.

steps.title: בית הלל: Then he should have said it differently
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reject רב פפא's reading because of how the man worded his statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל say: If so, he should have said 'that comes out first.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why בית הלל do not accept this reading. They argue that if the man meant the first of his black bulls, he would have worded it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית הלל, the wording 'שיצא בראשון' would mean 'the first of the black ones to come out.' The man did not say that. So בית הלל understand him as meaning the very first bull of any color, and if a white bull came out first, his words did not come true.

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
If so,
he should have said 'that comes out as the first [of them].'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why בית הלל disagree with the reading given in Steps 8 and 10.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The man did not use the wording that would mean 'first of the black ones.'
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב פפא, the argument is about how to read the man's words. בית שמאי read 'first' as the first black bull. בית הלל read it as the first bull of any kind.

steps.title: רבא from Barnish: This is not a mistake at all
steps.stepSummary: רבא מברניש asks רב אשי why this is called a mistaken consecration, since the man got exactly what he meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא from Barnish said to רב אשי: Is this a mistaken consecration? It is an intentional consecration!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מברניש challenges רב פפא's explanation. If the man meant the first black bull, there was no mistake, so why does the משנה treat this as הקדש בטעות?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole משנה is supposed to be about הקדש בטעות. But under רב פפא, the man's plan worked out exactly as he wanted. So the case no longer looks like a mistake at all.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא from the town of Barnish

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִבַּרְנִישׁ לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava from Barnish said to Rav Ashi:
Is this a mistaken consecration?
It is an intentional consecration!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִבַּרְנִישׁ לְרַב אָשֵׁי: הַאי הֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּטָעוּת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's explanation from Step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under his reading, the man got exactly what he meant, so the case cannot be about a mistaken consecration.

steps.title: It is called a mistake because his first words were misleading
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that his wording misled people, so the case is still called a mistaken consecration.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא מברניש. The case is called a mistake because the man's words, as first heard, sounded like he meant any first bull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'mistake' was in how he spoke, not in what he meant. His words gave a wrong impression. This answer keeps רב פפא's explanation, which means that even בית שמאי agree a true mistaken consecration does not work.

phrases.english: Because he made misleading
his first statement.
phrases.notes: Read together: his opening words sounded like he meant the very first bull of any color.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא מברניש's challenge from Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was no mistake at all, since he got what he meant.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mistake was in his wording, which gave a wrong impression.

steps.title: Do בית שמאי really hold a mistaken consecration does not work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the idea that בית שמאי hold a mistaken consecration does not take effect. It starts quoting a משנה about a נזיר whose vow was released.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do בית שמאי really hold that a mistaken consecration is not a consecration? But we learned in a משנה: If someone vowed to be a נזיר, asked the חכמים, and they released his vow, and he had already set aside an animal, it goes out and grazes with the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the conclusion of רב פפא's approach and begins quoting a משנה about a released נזיר vow. The case continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא, even בית שמאי agree that a true mistaken consecration does not work. The גמרא now asks whether that is really their view. It brings a משנה where an animal set aside for a נזיר's offering becomes ordinary again once the vow is released. The rest of the משנה, which comes next, shows how this case fits into the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked the חכמים to release his vow
An animal already set aside for an offering
It grazes with the flock, meaning it is an ordinary animal

steps.confusionAlert: The quote is not finished here. The part of the משנה that speaks about בית שמאי comes in Step 15, so wait for it before deciding how this challenges the question.

phrases.english: And do Beit Shammai hold
that a mistaken consecration is not a consecration?
But didn't we learn:
One who vowed to be a nazir
and asked the Sages, and they released him,
and he had an animal set aside,
phrases.notes: He had set it aside for one of his נזיר offerings before the vow was released.

phrases.english: it goes out and grazes with the flock.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּטָעוּת לָא הָוֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 13 shows that even בית שמאי reject a true mistaken consecration, the גמרא tests that idea against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that בית שמאי hold a mistaken consecration does not take effect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה about a released נזיר vow, בית הלל push בית שמאי with the claim that the animal goes free because it was a mistaken consecration. That argument assumes בית שמאי normally hold a mistaken consecration does take effect, which contradicts Step 13. Step 15 spells out this inference.

steps.title: בית הלל's challenge shows בית שמאי think a mistaken consecration takes effect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה. בית הלל argue against בית שמאי from a mistaken consecration, which implies that בית שמאי hold a הקדש בטעות is holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: Don't you agree that this is a mistaken consecration, and so the animal goes out and grazes with the flock? This shows that בית שמאי hold a mistaken consecration does take effect!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the משנה it began quoting in step 14. It then draws an inference from that משנה that challenges the earlier claim about בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל used the case of the released נזיר as an argument against בית שמאי. They would only argue this way if בית שמאי held that a mistaken consecration takes effect. That contradicts the earlier idea that בית שמאי hold it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't you agree…? (used to push the other side with a case they accept)
It goes out and grazes with the flock, meaning it is an ordinary animal again
By implication, from this we can learn

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
Don't you agree
that it is a mistaken consecration,
and so it goes out and grazes with the flock?!
This implies that Beit Shammai hold
that a mistaken consecration is a consecration!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה quote begun in step 14 and states the challenge drawn from it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית שמאי hold a mistaken consecration does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית הלל's argument only works if בית שמאי hold that a mistaken consecration takes effect.

steps.title: בית הלל misunderstood בית שמאי's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בית הלל wrongly thought בית שמאי's reason was that a mistaken consecration takes effect. בית שמאי replied that their reason was only that the man's first words were misleading.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it was בית הלל who made a mistake. They thought בית שמאי's reason was that a mistaken consecration takes effect. בית שמאי told them: Our reason is not about a mistaken consecration. It is because his first statement was misleading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 15. בית הלל's argument came from misunderstanding בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference about בית שמאי rests only on how בית הלל understood them, and בית הלל were wrong. בית שמאי's real reason in the black bull case is that the man meant what he got, but his words misled people. So בית שמאי never said a true mistaken consecration takes effect.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, בית שמאי do not say a true mistaken consecration takes effect. The black bull case only gets that name because the man's wording was misleading.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל הוּא דְּקָא טָעוּ,
phrases.english: Rather, it is Beit Hillel who erred;
they thought that Beit Shammai's reason
was because a mistaken consecration is a consecration.
And Beit Shammai said to them:
It is not because of a mistaken consecration;
rather, it is because he made his first statement misleading.
phrases.notes: This goes back to the black bull case from step 13. He got what he meant, but his words misled people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל הוּא דְּקָא טָעוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the inference: the premise came from בית הלל's misunderstanding.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל's challenge shows that בית שמאי hold a mistaken consecration takes effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי's ruling is based on misleading wording, not on a true mistaken consecration.

steps.title: A new challenge begins from another משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks whether בית שמאי really hold that a mistaken consecration does not take effect. It starts quoting a משנה about people walking along the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do בית שמאי really hold that a mistaken consecration is not a consecration? Come and hear: There were people walking along the road…
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge against the conclusion of step 16. It is setting up the next move by beginning to quote a משנה that will be used as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 concluded that בית שמאי hold a mistaken consecration does not take effect. Now the גמרא doubts this and brings a different משנה as evidence. Only the opening words are quoted so far, so the actual proof comes next.

phrases.english: And do Beit Shammai hold
that a mistaken consecration is not a consecration?
Come and hear:
If people were walking along the road,
phrases.notes: This is the start of a משנה found later, on 32b. The rest of it comes next.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּטָעוּת לָא הָוֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ? תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 16 with a new source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that בית שמאי hold a mistaken consecration does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different משנה (still being quoted) will suggest that בית שמאי treat a mistaken consecration as valid.
